title: Windows platform security for AI agents
attributed_claim_summary: Microsoft described proposed Windows process and session isolation for agent execution, including restricted file/network access, separate agent sessions and distinct identities.
evidence_or_event: First-party June 2, 2026 Windows Developer Blog article; describes preview plans and claimed platform controls, with exact feature availability varying by release.
limitations: Vendor architecture/preview descriptions are not third-party security validation, universal availability or proof that agents are safe; capability and deployment status must be retested against actual platform versions.
research_relevance: Explicitly test authorization scope and isolation overhead for agents that read, write and call external tools, separate from code-generation output correctness.
practical_experiment: Run benign synthetic file/network-policy violation tests in an isolated disposable environment and record blocked actions, false denials and task-time overhead by OS version.
